chunks: And in the narration of Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, he said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man buys a slave; to whom does his wealth belong? So he said: If the seller knew that he had wealth, then it belongs to the buyer; and if he did not know, then it belongs to the seller.
ai.seo_question: When a person buys a slave, does the slave’s existing wealth belong to the buyer or the seller?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the property of a purchased slave in a sale transaction. It states that if the seller knew the slave possessed wealth, that wealth transfers to the buyer; if the seller did not know, it remains the seller's.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3816 - In a narration from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, he said: "I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who buys a slave, who does the wealth of the slave belong to?"
Imam (as) replied: "If the seller knew that the slave had wealth, then it belongs to the buyer. However, if the seller was unaware, then it belongs to the seller."
